title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: Anomaly detection methods struggle with data exhibiting varying local densities, where distance-based methods miss local anomalies and density-based methods require careful parameter selection and incur quadratic time complexity. SVEAD constructs an ensemble of random Voronoi diagrams by sampling anchors, scores points by normalized cell-relative distance weighted by local scale, and averages scores across partitions. Across 45 ADBench datasets it achieves the highest average AUC-ROC (0.8538) and AUC-PR (0.5000) among 12 baselines, including 0.9339 AUC-ROC on cardio, while maintaining linear time and constant space complexity.

approach: Route is paper_only with no author repository on disk (only an uncloned anonymous.4open.science link), so SVEAD is reimplemented from the paper: for each of t=100 partitions, sample m anchors uniformly without replacement, assign every point to its nearest anchor in standardized feature space (implicit Voronoi, no cell boundaries), score each point as (delta/delta_max) * delta_mean inside its cell, skip singleton cells, and average the per-partition scores. The match target is C1: AUC-ROC 0.9339 on ADBench cardio (1831 samples, 21 features, 176 anomalies); the dataset is fetched at runtime through a validated fallback chain (ADBench GitHub raw -> OpenML cardiotocography -> UCI Cardiotocography), all of which reduce to exactly the same 1831x21 table with 176 positives, and a hard validation gate asserts that shape before any scoring. The m hyperparameter is grid-searched over {2,4,...,256} with 5 seeded repeats per value and t=100, matching the paper's protocol (R7, R8); we report both the label-tuned best m and the full m-curve so the +/-0.0189 tolerance band is interpretable, plus AUC-PR (C2) for free from the same runs. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (GPU 500k-instance scalability) are explicitly out of scope on this CPU-only machine and are flagged as 'not reproduced' in the output.
steps: Install/verify deps: `pip install numpy scipy pandas scikit-learn matplotlib requests tqdm openpyxl xlrd`; confirm sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml and sklearn.metrics imports succeed.

Write svead/data.py with a priority loader and an on-disk cache at data/cardio.npz: (1) local cache; (2) ADBench GitHub — GET https://api.github.com/repos/Minqi824/ADBench/git/trees/main?recursive=1, find any path containing 'cardio' ending in .csv/.npz/.arff, download via raw.githubusercontent.com; (3) sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml(data_id=1466) or name='cardiotocography' — take the 21 feature columns, keep rows with NSP in {1,3}, label = (NSP == 3); (4) UCI fallback https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/193/cardiotocography.zip -> CTG.xls, same 21-feature/NSP filter.

Validate the loaded table in svead/data.py: assert X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, mean(y) ~= 0.0961, no NaN/inf (assumption A6); if any assertion fails on a fallback source, log the mismatch into the provenance dict and continue, because the source is then not guaranteed to be the ADBench cardio table.

Write svead/svead_core.py: sample_anchors(X, m, rng) -> unique row indices (R1); assign_cells(X, A, chunk_rows) -> (cell_ids, delta) using chunked Euclidean distance and argmin with lowest-index tie-break (R2, R11); cell_stats -> per-cell delta_max and delta_mean computed for all points before any scoring (R4); score_partition -> s = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean with NaN for singleton cells and a delta_max == 0 guard (R3, R5); svead_score(X, m, t, seed) -> nanmean over t partitions, 0 if all NaN, plus diagnostics (cell-size histogram, skipped fraction, per-partition seconds) (R6, R12).

Write svead/metrics.py: roc_auc_score wrapper, average_precision_score (primary AUC-PR), trapezoidal precision_recall_curve AUC (secondary), and summarize(list) -> mean/std/min/max; all functions take scores first and labels second so labels are consumed only post-prediction (R9, R10).

Run the smoke test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py`. Part A: synthetic 300x6 with 10% Gaussian outliers, m=4, t=3 -> assert finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8. Part B: real cardio, m=8, t=5 -> assert score shape (1831,), deterministic repeat for the same seed, total runtime < 60 s.

Run the pre-full-run intermediate checks below (dataset signature, standardization stats, anchor uniqueness, cell-size/skip diagnostics, a kNN-distance and IsolationForest sanity baseline, single-run timing extrapolation).

Write experiments/run_cardio.py: outer loop over m in the 8-value grid, inner loop over the 5 seeds, each run calling svead_score on the standardized matrix with t=100, recording AUC-ROC, AUC-PR (both variants), wall time, skipped-point fraction and cell statistics; append rows to results/per_m_table.csv and dump raw per-run records to results/raw_cardio.json.

Launch the full suite: `python experiments/run_cardio.py`; after the first two m values finish, check that the extrapolated total stays inside the budget (expected total is only a few minutes because the per-run cost is ~0.1-3 s at these sizes) and only then let it complete.

Select best m = argmax of mean AUC-ROC across the 5 seeds; compute mean/std for AUC-ROC and AUC-PR at that m, and also record the fixed-m=128 (A3 fallback) result and the full m-curve for sensitivity.

Write reproduce.py: load data from cache, reuse or regenerate results/raw_cardio.json, run selection, then write results/metrics.json with (a) C1 value vs 0.9339 with the 0.0189 band and PASS/FAIL verdict, (b) C2 value vs 0.5356, (c) per-m table and per-repeat spreads, (d) dataset provenance and validation flags, (e) timing, (f) the assumption ledger entries applied, (g) an explicit not_reproduced block for C3, C4, C5 and C6 (45-dataset average and GPU/500k scalability are out of scope on CPU).

Run the final entrypoint `python reproduce.py` and read results/metrics.json; report the reproduced C1 with its spread, label the overall verdict partially_reproduced, and never present C3-C6 as reproduced.
smoke_test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py` — synthesizes 300x6 data with 10% outliers at m=4, t=3 and asserts finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8; then scores the full 1831x21 cardio table at m=8, t=5, asserting shape (1831,), reproducible scores for a repeated seed, and under 60 s wall clock. This exercises download -> standardize -> anchor sampling -> nearest-anchor assignment -> cell stats -> scoring -> averaging -> AUC end to end on a few seconds of compute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset signature: X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, anomaly rate 0.0961, zero NaN/inf, and the 21 UCI/ADBench feature names present — abort or flag loudly if a fallback source yields different counts (e.g. 2126 rows means the suspect class was not filtered).
Standardization: after StandardScaler, per-column mean ~ 0 (|mean| < 1e-9) and std ~ 1 for all 21 columns; confirm the scaler is fit with no label access.
Anchor sampling: for every m in the grid and every seed, sampled anchor indices are distinct and len == m (requirement R1), verified on 20 random (m, seed) pairs.

Cell diagnostics: for m=256 on n=1831, singleton cells must be essentially zero and skipped-point fraction < 0.5%; log non-empty cell count, max/mean cell size, and skipped fraction for every (m, seed).

Score sanity: all scores finite and >= 0; distribution roughly right-skewed with a handful of large scores matching injected/synthetic outliers; Spearman correlation with a trivial 1-NN mean-distance baseline is clearly positive.

Sanity baselines on cardio: sklearn IsolationForest(n_estimators=100, random_state=1) and a global kNN mean-distance score; both should land roughly in 0.65-0.85 AUC-ROC — if SVEAD cannot beat them, the reimplementation is wrong, not the paper.
No-cell-means-0 check: with the chosen cell_stats_scope (anchor included at distance 0), delta_mean must still be > 0 for every non-singleton cell; assert this before the full run.

Timing probe: time one full run at m=256, t=100 -> extrapolate the whole 40-run grid; if the extrapolation exceeds ~25 minutes, drop to 3 repeats and/or m in {8,16,32,64,128} (documented as a reduced protocol).
Determinism: two back-to-back runs with identical (m, seed) produce bitwise-identical score vectors.
budget_plan: Total ~90 min on CPU. Setup and data acquisition 15 min (pip installs, the ADBench/OpenML/UCI fallback chain, cache write, dataset-signature validation). Implementation of svead/data.py, svead/svead_core.py and svead/metrics.py 20 min. Smoke test and intermediate checks 10 min (including the IsolationForest/kNN sanity baselines and the timing probe). Full cardio grid 25 min reserved though expected ~5-10 min (8 m values x 5 seeds x t=100 on a 1831x21 matrix; each run is only a few seconds, so sum over m of m makes the whole grid roughly 2x the cost of a single m=256 run per seed). Final reproduce.py + metrics.json writing and interpretation 10 min. Contingency: if a run ever exceeds the projection, first cut repeats from 5 to 3, then narrow the m grid to four values, always recording the reduced protocol in results/metrics.json. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (500k-instance CPU/GPU timing) are deliberately not scheduled.

"""Load and validate the ADBench `cardio` dataset.

Priority chain (first hit wins):
  1. workspace-local data/ copies from an earlier run of this code,
  2. the shared REPRO_DATA_CACHE directory (checked for known ADBench filenames),
  3. direct download from the official ADBench repository (Minqi824/ADBench).

The ADBench artifact `adbench/datasets/Classical/6_cardio.npz` is exactly the
table the paper's Table 3 lists for cardio (1831 samples, 21 features, 176
anomalies, 9.61% anomaly rate).  Its features are already per-column
standardised (col mean 0, col std 1), so no extra scaling is applied
(assumption A11 in state/assumption_ledger.json).

Labels are returned separately and are never touched by the scoring code.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import urllib.request

import numpy as np

ADBENCH_RAW_URL = (
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Minqi824/ADBench/main/"
    "adbench/datasets/Classical/6_cardio.npz"
)
ADBENCH_MD5 = "3724aeab845964e929fd8d3d95475490"

# Paper Table 3, row cardio (page 12).
DATASET_SIGNATURE = {
    "n_samples": 1831,
    "n_features": 21,
    "n_anomalies": 176,
    "anomaly_rate": 0.0961,
}

_CANDIDATE_NAMES = ("6_cardio.npz", "cardio_adbench.npz", "cardio.npz")


def _md5(path):
    h = hashlib.md5()
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        for block in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(block)
    return h.hexdigest()


def _candidate_paths():
    """Local data dir first, then every directory in REPRO_DATA_CACHE."""
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    local = os.path.join(here, "data")
    cache_env = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", "")
    dirs = [local]
    if cache_env:
        # REPRO_DATA_CACHE may itself hold the files or point at a parent dir.
        dirs.append(cache_env)
        root = cache_env
        for _ in range(3):
            root = os.path.dirname(root)
            if root and root not in dirs:
                dirs.append(root)
    paths = []
    for d in dirs:
        for name in _CANDIDATE_NAMES:
            p = os.path.join(d, name)
            if p not in paths and os.path.isfile(p):
                paths.append(p)
    return paths


def _download(dest):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dest), exist_ok=True)
    req = urllib.request.Request(ADBENCH_RAW_URL, headers={"User-Agent": "repro-svead"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300) as resp:
        blob = resp.read()
    if hashlib.md5(blob).hexdigest() != ADBENCH_MD5:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "downloaded ADBench cardio artifact has unexpected md5 %s"
            % hashlib.md5(blob).hexdigest()
        )
    with open(dest, "wb") as fh:
        fh.write(blob)
    return dest


def load_cardio(verbose: bool = True):
    """Return (X float64 (1831,21), y int64 {0,1} (1831,), provenance dict)."""
    provenance = {
        "dataset": "cardio",
        "source_repo": "https://github.com/Minqi824/ADBench",
        "artifact": "adbench/datasets/Classical/6_cardio.npz",
        "url": ADBENCH_RAW_URL,
        "expected_md5": ADBENCH_MD5,
    }
    src = None
    for p in _candidate_paths():
        digest = _md5(p)
        provenance.setdefault("candidates_checked", []).append(
            {"path": p, "md5": digest, "matches_official": digest == ADBENCH_MD5}
        )
        if digest == ADBENCH_MD5:
            src = p
            break
        # shape-valid but different bytes: keep as a last resort
        if src is None:
            src = p
    if src is None:
        local = os.path.join(
            os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
            "data",
            "cardio_adbench.npz",
        )
        src = _download(local)
        cache_env = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", "")
        if cache_env:
            try:
                with open(src, "rb") as fh:
                    blob = fh.read()
                mirror = os.path.join(cache_env, "6_cardio.npz")
                if not os.path.exists(mirror):
                    os.makedirs(cache_env, exist_ok=True)
                    with open(mirror, "wb") as fh:
                        fh.write(blob)
            except OSError:
                pass
    provenance["resolved_path"] = src
    provenance["resolved_md5"] = _md5(src)

    raw = np.load(src)
    X = np.asarray(raw["X"], dtype=np.float64)
    y = np.asarray(raw["y"]).astype(np.int64).ravel()

    ok = (
        X.shape == (DATASET_SIGNATURE["n_samples"], DATASET_SIGNATURE["n_features"])
        and int(y.sum()) == DATASET_SIGNATURE["n_anomalies"]
        and not np.isnan(X).any()
        and not np.isinf(X).any()
    )
    provenance["validation"] = {
        "shape": list(X.shape),
        "n_anomalies": int(y.sum()),
        "anomaly_rate": round(float(y.mean()), 6),
        "n_nan": int(np.isnan(X).sum()),
        "n_inf": int(np.isinf(X).sum()),
        "md5_matches_official_adbench": provenance["resolved_md5"] == ADBENCH_MD5,
        "signature_ok": bool(ok),
    }
    if not ok:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "cardio table does not match the paper signature: %s" % provenance["validation"]
        )
    if verbose:
        print(
            "[data] cardio: X=%s, anomalies=%d (%.2f%%), source=%s%s"
            % (
                X.shape,
                int(y.sum()),
                100.0 * y.mean(),
                src,
                " (official ADBench md5 verified)" if provenance["resolved_md5"] == ADBENCH_MD5 else " (md5 MISMATCH)",
            )
        )
    return X, y, provenance


if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover
    X, y, prov = load_cardio()
    print(json.dumps(provenance, indent=2))

"""Core SVEAD algorithm, reimplemented from the paper (arXiv:2601.03664).

Sections 4.1-4.4 + Algorithm 1:
  * per partition, sample m anchors uniformly WITHOUT replacement (R1),
  * assign every point to its nearest anchor (Euclidean); no explicit cell
    boundaries are ever built - membership only, via nearest-anchor queries
    (R2, R11),
  * per cell compute delta_max = max ||x - a|| and delta_mean = mean ||x - a||
    over the points assigned to that cell, anchor included with distance 0,
    before any scoring (R4),
  * within-cell score s = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean (Eqs. 2-3, R3);
    a point whose cell holds only the anchor (|C_i| = 1) is skipped for this
    partition (R5); a degenerate cell with delta_max == 0 scores 0,
  * final score = arithmetic mean over the t partitions (Eq. 5, R6).  A point
    skipped by some partitions is averaged over the partitions that scored it
    (assumption A12); the literal Algorithm-1 line-20 variant (sum / t) is
    returned alongside for sensitivity.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

CHUNK_ROWS = 8192


def sample_anchors(n: int, m: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    """R1: m distinct row indices, uniform without replacement."""
    m = int(min(m, n))
    idx = rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False)
    assert len(np.unique(idx)) == len(idx), "anchors must be distinct"
    return idx


def assign_cells(X: np.ndarray, A: np.ndarray, chunk_rows: int = CHUNK_ROWS):
    """Nearest-anchor assignment (implicit Voronoi, R2/R11).

    Returns (cell (n,) int64, delta (n,) float64): cell index of the nearest
    anchor and the Euclidean distance to it.  argmin breaks distance ties by
    the lowest anchor index (assumption A5), matching the `<=` in Eq. (1).
    """
    n = X.shape[0]
    m = A.shape[0]
    cell = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int64)
    delta = np.empty(n, dtype=np.float64)
    for s in range(0, n, chunk_rows):
        e = min(n, s + chunk_rows)
        diff = X[s:e, None, :].astype(np.float64) - A[None, :, :].astype(np.float64)
        d2 = np.einsum("ijk,ijk->ij", diff, diff, optimize=True)
        j = np.argmin(d2, axis=1)  # lowest index on ties
        cell[s:e] = j
        delta[s:e] = np.sqrt(d2[np.arange(e - s), j])
    return cell, delta


def cell_stats(cell: np.ndarray, delta: np.ndarray, m: int):
    """R4: per-cell delta_max and delta_mean over all assigned points.

    The anchor itself belongs to its cell with distance 0, so it is included
    in the mean (assumption A15) - exactly the x' in C_i of Eq. (2).
    """
    size = np.bincount(cell, minlength=m).astype(np.float64)
    dmax = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.float64)
    np.maximum.at(dmax, cell, delta)
    dmean = np.bincount(cell, weights=delta, minlength=m) / np.maximum(size, 1.0)
    return dmax, dmean, size


def score_partition(X: np.ndarray, A: np.ndarray, chunk_rows: int = CHUNK_ROWS):
    """Eqs. (2)-(3) for one partition: s = (delta/delta_max) * delta_mean.

    Singleton cells (|C_i| == 1) yield NaN -> the point is skipped in this
    partition (R5).  Cells with delta_max == 0 but >1 member (duplicated
    points) yield 0.0.
    """
    cell, delta = assign_cells(X, A, chunk_rows)
    dmax, dmean, size = cell_stats(cell, delta, A.shape[0])
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        s = (delta / dmax[cell]) * dmean[cell]
    s[np.isnan(s)] = 0.0  # delta_max == 0 degenerate cells
    s[size[cell] == 1.0] = np.nan  # R5: singleton cell -> skip
    return cell, size, s


def svead_score(
    X: np.ndarray,
    m: int,
    t: int = 100,
    seed: int = 1,
    chunk_rows: int = CHUNK_ROWS,
    return_diagnostics: bool = False,
):
    """Ensemble score f(x) = mean_k s^(k)(x) (Eq. 5, R6).

    Per-partition RNG streams are derived deterministically from
    (seed, m, partition index) via numpy's default_rng([seed, m, k])
    (assumption A14), so repeated runs with the same seed are bitwise
    identical and the 5 repeats of the paper's protocol use seeds 1..5.
    """
    X = np.ascontiguousarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
    n = X.shape[0]
    acc = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.float64)
    cnt = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.int64)
    skipped_points = 0
    cell_sizes = []

    for k in range(int(t)):
        rng = np.random.default_rng([int(seed), int(m), int(k)])
        idx = sample_anchors(n, m, rng)
        A = X[idx]
        cell, size, s = score_partition(X, A, chunk_rows)
        valid = ~np.isnan(s)
        acc[valid] += s[valid]
        cnt += valid
        skipped_points += int((~valid).sum())
        cell_sizes.append(float(size.max()))

    mean_over_scored = np.where(cnt > 0, acc / np.maximum(cnt, 1), 0.0)
    literal_sum_over_t = acc / float(t)  # Algorithm 1 line 20 variant

    if not return_diagnostics:
        return mean_over_scored

    diag = {
        "n": n,
        "m": int(m),
        "t": int(t),
        "seed": int(seed),
        "skipped_point_partitions": skipped_points,
        "skipped_fraction": skipped_points / float(n * t),
        "points_with_no_score": int((cnt == 0).sum()),
        "max_cell_size_mean_over_partitions": float(np.mean(cell_sizes)),
    }
    return mean_over_scored, {
        "mean_over_scored": mean_over_scored,
        "literal_sum_over_t": literal_sum_over_t,
        "diagnostics": diag,
    }

def main() -> int:
    t0 = time.time()
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)

    # ---- Part A: synthetic ----
    normal = rng.normal(size=(270, 6))
    outliers = rng.normal(size=(30, 6)) * 6.0 + 8.0
    Xs = np.vstack([normal, outliers])
    ys = np.r_[np.zeros(270, dtype=int), np.ones(30, dtype=int)]
    scores = svead_score(Xs, m=4, t=3, seed=1)
    assert scores.shape == (300,), scores.shape
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(scores)) and np.all(scores >= 0)
    auc = auc_roc(scores, ys)
    print(f"[smoke A] synthetic AUC-ROC={auc:.4f} (expect > 0.8)")
    assert auc > 0.8, auc

    # ---- Part B: real cardio, determinism ----
    X, y, prov = load_cardio()
    s1 = svead_score(X, m=8, t=5, seed=7)
    s2 = svead_score(X, m=8, t=5, seed=7)
    assert s1.shape == (1831,)
    assert np.array_equal(s1, s2), "same-seed runs must be bitwise identical"
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(s1)) and np.all(s1 >= 0)
    auc1 = auc_roc(s1, y)
    print(f"[smoke B] cardio m=8 t=5 AUC-ROC={auc1:.4f}, AUC-PR={auc_pr(s1, y):.4f}")
    assert s1.max() > s1.min(), "degenerate scores"

    # a point in a big dense cluster must score lower than a far outlier
    dt, elapsed = None, time.time() - t0
    print(f"[smoke] total wall clock {elapsed:.1f}s (limit 60 s)")
    assert elapsed < 60
    print("SMOKE OK")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Full cardio protocol (paper Section 5.1).

Grid search m over {2^1, ..., 2^8} with ensemble size t=100, 5 repeats
(seeds 1..5), AUC-ROC / AUC-PR computed only after scores exist.

Writes results/per_m_table.csv and results/raw_cardio.json.
Selection: m* = argmax_m mean AUC-ROC over the 5 repeats (assumptions A3/A10).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

from svead.data import DATASET_SIGNATURE, load_cardio
from svead.metrics import auc_pr, auc_pr_trapz, auc_roc
from svead.svead_core import svead_score

M_GRID = [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256]  # {2^1, ..., 2^8} (R7)
SEEDS = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]  # 5 repeats (R8)
T_ENSEMBLE = 100  # R7

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
RESULTS = HERE / "results"


def run_grid(X, y, m_grid=None, seeds=None, t=T_ENSEMBLE, verbose=True):
    m_grid = M_GRID if m_grid is None else m_grid
    seeds = SEEDS if seeds is None else seeds
    rows = []
    for m in m_grid:
        for seed in seeds:
            t0 = time.time()
            scores, extra = svead_score(
                X, m=m, t=t, seed=seed, return_diagnostics=True
            )
            wall = time.time() - t0
            diag = extra["diagnostics"]
            # A12 sensitivity: Algorithm-1 literal sum/t aggregation
            auc_roc_literal = auc_roc(extra["literal_sum_over_t"], y)
            row = {
                "m": m,
                "seed": seed,
                "t": t,
                "auc_roc": auc_roc(scores, y),
                "auc_pr": auc_pr(scores, y),
                "auc_pr_trapz": auc_pr_trapz(scores, y),
                "auc_roc_literal_sum_over_t": auc_roc_literal,
                "wall_seconds": wall,
                "skipped_fraction": diag["skipped_fraction"],
                "points_with_no_score": diag["points_with_no_score"],
                "max_cell_size_mean": diag["max_cell_size_mean_over_partitions"],
            }
            rows.append(row)
            if verbose:
                print(
                    "[grid] m=%3d seed=%d  AUC-ROC %.4f  AUC-PR %.4f  (%.2fs)"
                    % (m, seed, row["auc_roc"], row["auc_pr"], wall),
                    flush=True,
                )
    return rows


def summarize_by_m(rows):
    """Mean/std per m and the m* selected by mean AUC-ROC."""
    by_m = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_m.setdefault(r["m"], []).append(r)
    summary = []
    for m in sorted(by_m):
        rs = by_m[m]
        roc = np.array([r["auc_roc"] for r in rs])
        pr = np.array([r["auc_pr"] for r in rs])
        summary.append(
            {
                "m": m,
                "n_runs": len(rs),
                "auc_roc_mean": float(roc.mean()),
                "auc_roc_std": float(roc.std(ddof=1)),
                "auc_pr_mean": float(pr.mean()),
                "auc_pr_std": float(pr.std(ddof=1)),
                "auc_roc_values": [float(v) for v in roc],
                "auc_pr_values": [float(v) for v in pr],
                "total_seconds": float(sum(r["wall_seconds"] for r in rs)),
            }
        )
    best = max(summary, key=lambda s: s["auc_roc_mean"])
    return summary, best


def main(force: bool = False):
    RESULTS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    raw_path = RESULTS / "raw_cardio.json"
    X, y, prov = load_cardio()

    if raw_path.exists() and not force:
        print(f"[run_cardio] reusing cached {raw_path}")
        blob = json.loads(raw_path.read_text())
        rows = blob["runs"]
    else:
        t0 = time.time()
        rows = run_grid(X, y)
        total = time.time() - t0
        print(f"[run_cardio] grid finished in {total:.1f}s")
        blob = {
            "dataset_provenance": prov,
            "dataset_signature": DATASET_SIGNATURE,
            "protocol": {
                "m_grid": M_GRID,
                "seeds": SEEDS,
                "t_ensemble": T_ENSEMBLE,
                "repeats": len(SEEDS),
                "scaling": "none beyond the ADBench artifact's own standardisation (A11)",
            },
            "total_wall_seconds": total,
            "runs": rows,
        }
        raw_path.write_text(json.dumps(blob, indent=2))

        with open(RESULTS / "per_m_table.csv", "w", newline="") as fh:
            w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=list(rows[0].keys()))
            w.writeheader()
            w.writerows(rows)

    summary, best = summarize_by_m(rows)
    print(
        "[run_cardio] best m=%d  mean AUC-ROC %.4f (+-%.4f)  mean AUC-PR %.4f"
        % (best["m"], best["auc_roc_mean"], best["auc_roc_std"], best["auc_pr_mean"])
    )
    return {"rows": rows, "summary": summary, "best": best, "provenance": prov, "raw": blob}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(force="--force" in sys.argv)

from __future__ import annotations

import platform
import time

import numpy as np


def measure(n: int, d: int, m_list, t: int = 100, seed: int = 0):
    from svead.svead_core import svead_score

    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    X = rng.normal(size=(n, d)).astype(np.float64)
    out = {
        "n_samples": n,
        "d": d,
        "t": t,
        "cpu": platform.processor() or platform.machine(),
        "python_threads_note": "single-process numpy (BLAS may use several cores)",
        "measurements": [],
    }
    for m in m_list:
        t0 = time.time()
        svead_score(X, m=m, t=t, seed=1)
        out["measurements"].append({"m": m, "wall_seconds": time.time() - t0})
    return out

audit_summary: The reproduction is a genuine paper-only reimplementation of SVEAD (anchor sampling, implicit nearest-anchor Voronoi assignment, (delta/delta_max)*delta_mean within-cell score, singleton skip, ensemble mean, t=100, grid over m in {2^1..2^8}, 5 repeats) evaluated on the md5-verified official ADBench cardio artifact (1831x21, 176 anomalies, 9.61%), so dataset, metric (AUC-ROC on all samples, unsupervised scoring with labels used only afterwards) and method all match the C1 target. The clean re-run deleted results/ and recomputed everything from the grid (110.7 s, log shows the full m-grid rerun); the reported 0.9310 +/- 0.0074 is a computed value, not a hard-coded or echoed paper number (the constants in reproduce.py are explicitly labelled reference values used only for the PASS/FAIL comparison). The only material protocol choice is that m* is picked by argmax of AUC-ROC over the same 5 labeled repeats (m*=2, the lower boundary of the paper's grid); this label-using grid search is the paper's stated protocol but is disclosed as high-risk assumptions A3/A10, and since AUC-ROC is monotone decreasing in m here, the reported number is essentially the best-of-grid value, which a reader should treat as an optimistic-but-in-protocol estimate. Residual deviation from 0.9339 is 0.0029, inside the 3-sigma tolerance, and is attributable to unspecified seeds (A4) and the unreported per-dataset m / preprocessing (A3, A11). The ensemble-averaging ambiguity (A12) is a non-issue because the skipped fraction is exactly zero at m=2, and the secondary Algorithm-1 variant agrees bitwise. C3/C4 and C6 are declared not reproduced and the C5 CPU reference measurement (14.1 s vs paper's <3 s on a different, faster CPU) is reported as hardware-dependent, not as a verdict; none of this affects the target's scaling (full grid, t=100, 5 seeds, no subsetting).

requirement_check.evidence: svead/svead_core.py sample_anchors uses rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False) with a distinctness assertion; per-partition rng = default_rng([seed,m,k]) (A14), so each of the t=100 partitions samples m anchors uniformly without replacement.
assign_cells computes chunked Euclidean squared distances to all m anchors and takes argmin (lowest index on ties, A5); membership only, no Voronoi geometry is built.
score_partition computes s = (delta / dmax[cell]) * dmean[cell], i.e. normalized cell-relative distance times the cell's mean anchor distance (Eqs. 2-3).
cell_stats precomputes dmax (np.maximum.at over deltas) and dmean (bincount(delta)/size) for every cell before any score is formed, matching Algorithm 1 lines 7-10.

Singleton cells are set to NaN and excluded from the per-point accumulator; the remaining partitions carry the average (Section 4.2). diagnostics.skipped_fraction is logged; at the selected m=2 it is 0.

Ensemble score is the mean of the partition scores that scored the point (Section 4.2 'rely on the remaining partitions'); the literal Algorithm-1 sum/t variant is also computed and both are bit-identical at m*=2 (skipped fraction 0), so the ambiguity in Eq. (5) cannot affect C1 (A12).
M_GRID=[2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256] with T_ENSEMBLE=100; m* selected as argmax of mean AUC-ROC over the 5 repeats -> m*=2, inside the paper's grid.
SEEDS=[1,2,3,4,5]; per-seed AUC-ROC values and ddof=1 std are reported (0.9310 +/- 0.0074).
svead/metrics.py uses sklearn roc_auc_score and average_precision_score (plus a trapezoidal PR variant); both AUC-ROC and AUC-PR are written to metrics.json.
metrics functions take (scores, labels) in that order; svead_core never receives y, so labels are consumed only after scoring.
No cell boundaries/vertices are ever constructed; only nearest-anchor queries (implicit Voronoi) are used.
Computation is chunked and vectorised with cost O(n*m*d*t); observed per-run wall time grows roughly linearly with m (0.03 s at m=2 to 16.1 s at m=256), consistent with linear complexity.
